findings.reason: the node must be told that `implementable_sections` and `plan_executable_remainder` both call the predicate directly (or that the predicate moves to a lower module), not that the schema calls into roadmap, otherwise the first implementation node hits an import cycle.
findings.text: §18 says the one implementation is the roadmap list-reader and that `_schema.plan_executable_remainder` is "expressed over it, returning the count of what `implementable_sections` lists", but `plan_executable_remainder` lives in `reckon/_schema.py` and `reckon/roadmap.py` already does `from reckon._schema import ...` (reckon/roadmap.py:21), so calling `roadmap.implementable_sections` from the schema is an upward import and a circular one; the same section two sentences later says all three readers call the new `_schema` predicate, which is the non-cyclic form — the text carries both and an implementer could land the cyclic one

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the three sections hide section identity, span location, prose slicing, per-section digesting and coverage behind a small interface: `plan_fingerprint` (unchanged return), the public `plan_headings`, the machinery-element predicate, and one classification predicate; the new helpers (`_section_digests`, the coverage predicate, the heading-walk rule) are private and each hides real work, not a forwarding pair.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §18 states the schema's count-reader is "expressed over" `roadmap.implementable_sections`, which would make reckon/_schema.py import reckon/roadmap.py while roadmap.py already imports `_schema` (reckon/roadmap.py:21), a cycle that contradicts the section's own "no import runs upward" claim.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1477, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; the three sections account for their additions and their non-retirements in their own text (§16 no public definition, §17 net two with `landed_section_ids` a move and no retirement because both existing readers keep callers, §18 one public predicate with nothing retirable because the three spellings keep distinct questions), and §16 states it reuses the existing plan-review-missing family rather than adding one.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the design sections name the machinery they extend and it exists: `_StructuredSectionSpanParser` and `structured_section_spans` (reckon/_plan_html.py:44,94), `section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates` (reckon/crew/routing.py:224,243), `landed_section_ids` (reckon/_store.py:1075), `roadmap.implementable_sections` (reckon/roadmap.py:106), `_schema.plan_executable_remainder` (reckon/_schema.py:788), and the AST census in `reckon/interface_counts.py`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — every retained thin surface states why it cannot be extended: `structured_section_spans` keeps its spans-only contract because reckon/_store.py:1685 and tests import it; the coverage predicate is stated as a join over two existing readers rather than a wrapper of `read_plan_review`; `_authored_prose` keeps its name doing real work (subtract protected spans, drop landed interiors, bucket by identity).
